sources.note: Section 2.3 'Prosody' (p. 5) covers only the extant languages: Murui and Mɨka dialects of Murui-Muina 'have fixed, word-initial stress (Wojtylak 2020a, b)', Mɨnɨka and Nɨpode 'exhibit meaningful tonal contrasts', Ocaina contrastive pitch / pitch accent, Nonuya pitch accent. MCT (Andoquero) forms are cited re-phonemicized in IPA with Martius's spelling in brackets (e.g. xɯ-ho-kkɯ [ɡöhóckö] 'my head', ku-rana-no [curánănŏ] 'my sister', Tupana mai pukka 'Deus fecit omne') and no comment on Martius's accent or breve marks; nothing on MCT stress or tone. Notes that Echeverri & Seifart's proto-Wito…

sources.note: No phonology content. sources.note: Nothing about Andoquero/Carapaná prosody. Its only stress statement is about Witoto proper, p. 396: 'Acento tónico: Se carga en la primera sílaba de la palabra, aunque los adverbios en kene, y dene, lo llevan en la penúltima. Si se trata de una palabra muy larga, la penúltima sílaba recibe un acento secundario.. según Kinder. Al contrario, en Kaime casi siempre se marca el acento en las sílabas antepenúltima y penúltima. En el vocabulario de Berner hay palabras agudas.' (second-hand, from Kinder 1936 and Koch-Grünberg 1906; belongs to Murui-Muina, not to ando1254). On the Carapaná list itself…

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1906. Les Indiens Ouitotos: étude linguistique. Journal de la Société des Américanistes n.s. 3(2): 157-189. (Introduction p. 161 on the Miranha-Carapaná-tapuyo; 'Indications phonétiques' pp. 161-162; 'IV. Vocabulaires du groupe Ouitoto' + 'Remarques' pp. 186-187; Appendice 'Liste comparative' pp. 188-189 with c. 46 Martius Carapaná items)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on the accent of the Carapaná (Andoquero) list. The 'Indications phonétiques' key (pp. 161-162) includes 'á = accent du mot', but it governs Koch-Grünberg's own Ouitoto-Káime transcription (and Berner's), not Martius's list, which he cites in 'transcription allemande' (p. 186). His 'Remarques' on the Miranha list are segmental/morphological only: 'Préfixes pronominaux: En langue Miranha et en Coëruna, les préfixes: ga-, go- (ca-, co-) et co-, cu-, servent à désigner les parties du corps humain..' and 'd, t en Käime devient tz (ts) en Miranha' (pp. 186-187).

sources.citation: von Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. I: Zur Ethnographie. Leipzig: Fleischer. ('Die Miranhas', pp. 534-544)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on pronunciation, accent or tone. The only linguistic remarks are that the two Miranha hordes differ in speech ('die zwei auch in der Sprache abweichenden Horden der Miranhas, am obern Yupurá, die Grossvogel- und die Schnacken-Indianer') and, p. 537, 'Wie sehr die Idiome derselben auseinandergehn, mag eine Vergleichung derselben***) darthun' pointing to the Bd. II wordlists; the rest of the chapter is ethnographic (dress, slaving, anthropophagy, basketry).

sources.citation: von Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp. 1863 [1867]. Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen (Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium). Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II. Erlangen/Leipzig: Fleischer. Wordlist "Miranha Carapana-Tapuya", pp. 277-279.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing stated. The list (c. 200 Latin-glossed items plus one sentence, elicited by Martius from chief João Manoel on the upper Yupurá, footnote p. 277) prints acute accents on most words (e.g. gakaikaná, nóhwi, göhóckö, ganoagá, gamaámi, retóbbi, máhwarĩ); accent position is variable (penultimate and final both frequent). The acute is explained only in the Tupi-dictionary orthographic note, vol. II p. 29: the accent 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen', with no statement that it applies to the Miranha lists.
